evals.prompt: Plan the next quarter for my newsletter. My project's AGENTS.md points my publications to ~/pubs/; this one is 'side-income-weekly'.
evals.expected_output: Should find the folder from AGENTS.md, read ~/pubs/side-income-weekly/profile.md (including its Defaults) and writing-guide.md first and judge every idea against the profile's reader job, owner job and one action. Should keep calendar.md in that publication's folder as the editorial calendar — one line per topic with its first publish date, formats, status and holder, under Coming up, Ideas and Published — and give each briefed topic its own folder under topics/ with a brief.md whose 'What this topic becomes' table lists each format, where it goes and its date, never writing inside the installed plugin. Should read the answers the profile's Defaults already give and ask only what's missing — the period and a cadence the writer can keep, then per topic the formats, where each goes, full copy or opening excerpt per cross-post platform and a date per format — offering the defaults as choices, and record the answers in each brief.
expectations: Reads profile.md and writing-guide.md from the folder AGENTS.md names
Scores ideas against the profile's purpose and reader
Asks only what the profile and request don't answer, offering the profile's Defaults as choices
Keeps calendar.md as one line per topic in its section, with each briefed topic in its own topics/<yyyy-mm>-<slug>/ folder and brief.md
Fills the brief's 'What this topic becomes' with each format, its destination and its date
Does not write the calendar inside the plugin

evals.prompt: Give me 60 blog post ideas, one for every variation of 'best credit card for X' — students, travel, cashback, bad credit, and so on — and I'll publish two a week.
evals.expected_output: Should warn that near-duplicate pieces per keyword variant and volume for its own sake match Google's scaled content abuse and search-engine-first warning signs. Should propose fewer, distinct pieces chosen from reader questions and search data, scored on fit and first-hand experience, at a cadence the writer can keep.
expectations: Flags near-duplicate keyword-variant pieces as a problem
Cites scaled content abuse or search-first signals
Proposes fewer distinct pieces scored on fit and experience
Sets a sustainable cadence with a buffer

evals.prompt: What should I write next for my developer blog? I don't want to guess.
evals.expected_output: Should gather ideas from evidence: reader questions in their own words, Search Console queries with impressions but no matching piece, Trends and autocomplete as relative signals, gaps from /cw:content-performance, and the writer's own recent work. Each idea kept with its source and scored before scheduling.
expectations: Draws ideas from reader questions and Search Console queries
Treats Trends as relative, not absolute volume
Includes gaps from the last performance review
Records each idea's source and scores it

evals.prompt: I want to start a 6-part series on building a budgeting app. Just schedule part 1 for Monday; I'll figure out the rest later.
evals.expected_output: Should plan the whole series before publishing part 1 — the parts, what each delivers on its own, links between parts — in a series/<series-slug>.md file with a parts table, and make sure each part stands alone for a reader arriving from search. Each part is its own topic folder, created when that part is briefed, with Series and Part in its brief. Should work back from publish dates through research, demo project, images, edit and review.
expectations: Plans all six parts before scheduling part 1, in a series/ file with a parts table
Makes each part its own topic, with Series and Part in its brief
Makes each part stand alone with links between parts
Works back from publish dates through the production steps, including the demo project
